prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: High-fidelity planning concept screenshot for Pino club onboarding; unapproved concept with fictional sample content.
Primary request: Produce a polished desktop landscape web application screenshot, approximately 1360 x 900 composition. The concept is "Browse, then request". It is an operational club directory with a list-detail workspace, not a marketing page or wizard.
Input image 1 is a visual style reference only. Preserve its compact navy header (#202c42), Segoe UI/system sans-serif typography, cobalt primary actions (#244d9e), white flat writing surfaces separated by thin #dce2ec rules, pale-blue selected rows (#e7edf6), and cool canvas (#f5f7fa). Do not carry over any tryout, player, roster, season, note, or team-placement content.
Composition: edge-to-edge screenshot with no device frame. Compact full-width navy header at top; "Pino." left, "Morgan Chen" and "Account" right; a small "Fictional sample" label. Main page inset around 32px horizontally. Heading "Find your club", supporting line "Choose the right organization before requesting access." Top right outlined secondary button "Create a club". Profile is already complete, so there is no profile form or progress stepper.
Main workspace begins below the heading with a fine outer rule and two adjacent white panes. Left pane approximately one third of the width. Right selected-club pane approximately two thirds. Keep square workspace corners, understated 6px button corners, ample readable space, strong navy headings, crisp text, and no shadows.
Left pane: small section heading "Clubs". Visible form label "Club name" above a search input containing the exact text "Northside"; minimal magnifying glass icon is acceptable. Three ruled results underneath. Each row is clickable and composed of a bold club name then sport and city/region on readable secondary lines. Row 1 is selected with pale-blue fill: "Northside FC", "Soccer", "Chicago, Illinois". Row 2: "Northside United", "Soccer", "Evanston, Illinois". Row 3: "Northside Juniors", "Soccer", "Milwaukee, Wisconsin". Use small chevrons at row ends if useful. No checkboxes. No counts.
Right pane: generous inset around 40px. Large selected-club heading "Northside FC". Supporting text "Soccer" and "Chicago, Illinois". A thin horizontal rule separates identity from access request. Below that rule show medium heading "Request access as a coach" and clear body text "A club administrator will review your request." Below the copy, a solid cobalt primary action labeled "Request to join". Under the action in smaller muted text: "You can belong to one club at a time." Keep the remaining white space calm and intentional. Do not add content below just to fill space.
Constraints: all visible content must be accurately spelled and legible. Exactly the three fictional club records specified. The listed club names and Morgan Chen are fictional sample data. The interface exposes only club name, sport, city/region. No member names in the results or details, no member counts, no player data, no club imagery, no fabricated logos, no branding claims, no subscription or pricing information. No equal choice cards, centered sequential wizard, decorative illustrations, gradients, drop shadows, floating widgets, or invented navigation. This is a clear list-detail pattern that matches the reference visual system.
